blocking.issue: The fail-open bound for derived ceilings leaves out the per-Node floor of one token that the owning Traffic management document applies. As a result the stated number understates real admission whenever 2 x requests < N_published. The Control-mode case of a Node with no count (clamp max(1, requests / 100)) has no row at all. This document owns the pack 8.8 bound, so a wrong number here is a design defect.
blocking.evidence: Line 353: "| Rate Limit, fail-open | Derived ceiling, OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-16 option (b) | At most N_serving / N_published × 2 × `requests` per aligned window (target) |". The Traffic management failure matrix says: "Unfloored buckets admit N_serving / N_published × 2 × limit per aligned window, one token per Node at least" and "fail-open admits N_countless × the clamp ... 10 × limit (hypothesis)". Worked case: `requests: 10` per `1s` on 100 Nodes gives max(1, 0.2) = 1 token per Node, so 100 per second (10 × limit), not the 20 the row states.
blocking.fix: Restate the row as 'At most N_serving × max(1, 2 × `requests` / N_published) per aligned window (target)' and show the 10-per-second-on-100-Nodes example. Add a row 'Rate Limit, fail-open | Control-mode Node without a count | At most N_countless × max(1, `requests` / 100) per window, plus the counted Nodes' share (target)'. blocking.issue: The post-commit queue drains its classes in strict table order, so cache invalidations sit behind cache stores. Under sustained store load the invalidation class, which is only 10% of the queue, fills up and drops. That defeats the reserved slice that Traffic management relies on, because an invalidation must not drop. Plugin writes can starve entirely.
blocking.evidence: Line 326: "Eight writers per Node drain the classes in table order, pipelining up to 64 writes per batch (target)." The table order (lines 321 to 324) is Quota refunds and Token Budget settlement, then Cache stores, then Cache invalidations, then Plugin writes. Traffic management says: "Generation bumps get a reserved 10% of that queue and one retry (target)" and "invalidations must not drop".
blocking.fix: Drain order: settlement first, then invalidations, then stores and Plugin writes. Use weighted round-robin between the last two, for example 4:1 (target), so no class waits longer than one batch interval. Add a bound: 'an invalidation waits at most one batch behind settlement (target)'. Add a CE-6 variant that saturates cache stores and asserts zero `cache_invalidate` drops.

blocking.issue: Unbounded memory. The Plugin-writes class of the post-commit queue has only an item cap and no byte cap, and neither this document nor WASM plugin system caps value size (WASM caps keys at 256 bytes only). The claim that caches and the queue add at most 128 MiB per Node is therefore false.
blocking.evidence: Line 324: "| Plugin writes | 9,600 items (target) | Drop per Plugin Policy |". Line 559: "these limits add at most 64 MiB for keys, 256 MiB for balancers and 128 MiB for caches and the queue (target)". WASM plugin system: "Limits (target): 256-byte keys, `ttlMillis` 1 ms to 24 h, 10,000 keys per Policy per Node per minute, one `onLog` write per request". No value limit is given. For example, 9,600 queued 1 MiB values hold about 9.4 GiB.
blocking.fix: Add a byte cap to the Plugin-writes class, for example 16 MiB (target), and to the settlement class. Propose a per-value cap for `state.write`, for example 64 KiB (target), as an Open question owned by wasm-plugin-system or through OQ-wasm-plugin-system-19. Recompute line 559 from every class's byte cap.

blocking.issue: Two capacity targets contradict each other. Autoscaling lets steady-state CPU reach 60%, yet the availability rule requires survivors to stay under 80% CPU after the largest zone is lost. With two zones, 60% becomes about 120%. With three zones it becomes about 90%. Only four or more zones satisfy both.
blocking.evidence: Line 141: "| CPU | Container CPU utilization | 60% over 2 minutes (target) |". Line 169: "A Cluster SHOULD run at least three Nodes in at least two zones (target), sized so that losing the largest zone keeps survivors under 80% CPU (target)."
blocking.fix: Derive the CPU scale-out threshold from the zone count: threshold = 80% × (Z - 1) / Z, which gives 40% for two zones and about 53% for three (target). Alternatively, require at least three zones with a 50% threshold, and state the formula in both places.

blocking.issue: The required Raft HA state diagram models fencing staleness as an alternative to candidacy instead of a condition that runs alongside it. A voter in a minority partition goes Follower to Candidate and loops in Candidate, so on this diagram it never becomes Stale and never sends Reconnect (rebalance). Its Nodes stay pinned to an isolated replica, which contradicts Control plane and GitOps: 'A replica without word from a leader for one election timeout ... is stale ... After 30 s stale (target) it sends Reconnect'. Both transitions also fire on the same timeout with hashicorp/raft defaults (1000 ms), so the diagram does not say which one wins.
blocking.evidence: Line 189: "Follower --> Candidate: no leader heartbeat within HeartbeatTimeout". Line 191: "Candidate --> Candidate: split vote or no majority, new election after ElectionTimeout". Line 194: "Follower --> Stale: leader contact lost for one election timeout". No transition leaves Candidate toward Stale or Rebalancing.
blocking.fix: Model fencing as a concurrent region: a Raft region (Follower, Candidate, Leader) beside a fencing region (Fresh, Stale, Rebalancing) whose clock runs on 'no leader contact' whatever the Raft state. Or add 'Candidate --> Stale: no leader for one election timeout' and 'Stale --> Rebalancing: stale for 30 s' for candidates too. State what a Candidate serves to its Nodes: the Stale rule.

blocking.issue: The inventory claims to be complete, but it omits per-Node state that the dependency documents and this document create. Acceptance criterion 3 requires every in-memory per-Node state, each with its bound and why losing it is safe.
blocking.evidence: Line 50: "This table is the complete inventory of in-memory per-Node state; new per-Node state needs a row here before it ships." These are missing: State client breakers per shard, the connections and in-flight call counter (the 8,192 ceiling, defined at line 330 of this document); Response Cache miss coalescing ("up to 4,096 keys (target)") and the revalidation queue ("256-entry queue"); the per-URI `Vary`-name LRU; the per-shard `INFO memory` readings behind store skipping; the first-seen budget counters; Semantic Cache per-Node concurrency caps; Plugin per-Policy key-rate counters ("10,000 keys per Policy per Node per minute"); and `/tap` buffers (Data plane Bounded resources).
blocking.fix: Add one row for each missing item, each with a bound, what rebuilds it and why losing it is safe. For example: 'State client breakers and connections | 2 + 8 per shard, 8,192 calls | New dials; breakers start closed | First calls pay one deadline, then the breaker reopens'. Or drop the word 'complete' and point to Data plane Bounded resources for the others.

blocking.issue: Some scale figures carry no (target) or (hypothesis) tag, which breaks the style guide section 4 rule.
blocking.evidence: Line 589: "| CE-9 | Scale from 10 to 100 Nodes in 2 minutes | Over-admission within the derived-ceiling bound | Planned (M2) |". Line 586: "| CE-12 | Hot key at 10 times one shard's capacity | Calls for it at most N × ceiling per window | Planned (M1) |".
blocking.fix: Tag each figure on its line: 'Scale from 10 to 100 Nodes in 2 minutes (target)' and 'Hot key at 10 times one shard's capacity, about 1,000,000 calls per second (hypothesis)'.

non_blocking.suggestion: The reason given for 'two Nodes on one host are unsupported' does not hold: the file lock is per ${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}, so two Nodes with separate data directories could both bind. The real reason is that SO_REUSEPORT and CBPF steering assume one Node per network namespace. Write it as 'Not planned' with that reason, and avoid the word '(un)supported'.

'Supported topologies are OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-2' uses 'Supported', which style guide section 4 reserves. Rephrase as 'The topologies the redis driver accepts are OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-2'.

The divided-Quota YAML puts a Bundle `Consumer` in the same stream as control-plane-only `Environment` and `Cluster`, which a Bundle rejects with RZ-CFG-017. Split it into two fences labeled 'Bundle file' and 'control directory or --environments file'.

OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-11 calls option (c) of OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-19 a pack 8.8 amendment. Option (c) persists the Node count under ${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}, so it amends pack 8.11. Name both sections.

'Tenants per Cell: At most 10% of tenants (target)' contradicts the single-Region topology of one Cell. Scope it to deployments with ten or more Cells. Also fix the arithmetic '1,000,000, 60% of 16 shards at about 100,000 each', which comes to 960,000.

'Connections per shard 10 × N_serving, 10,000 at 1,000 Nodes' equals the Redis and Valkey default maxclients at the Cell's Node ceiling. Make raising maxclients a MUST above about 900 Nodes. Also state which Cell ceiling binds first at realistic per-Node stateful request rates: at 5,000 State Store calls per second per Node (hypothesis), the 1,000,000-call ceiling binds at 200 Nodes.

Define the 8,192 in-flight State Store call ceiling as counting until reply or connection reset, not until the caller's timeout. rueidis cannot retract an auto-pipelined command already written, so abandoned calls still occupy ring slots during a CE-3 brownout. Also state how many half-open probe calls the breaker allows.

'Autoscaled Control-mode Clusters SHOULD declare per-Node ceilings' needs sizing guidance. A declared ceiling c fails open at N_serving × c, so c must be sized for the maximum autoscaled Node count (limit / N_max) to keep the bound at the limit.

The failover-lag row assumes the TAT rolls back. A key first written within the lag window is missing on the new primary and restarts GCRA with a full burst τ, which allows up to `requests` extra. Add that case. Also add the release document's case of a Node rolled back to N-1 after lazy migration, which admits up to 2x for one window.

hashicorp/raft randomizes the follower timeout between 1x and 2x HeartbeatTimeout, and election adds ElectionTimeout jitter, so 'about 1 to 2 s plus election round trips' is optimistic. Say 1 to 3 s plus round trips (hypothesis), or cite the research derivation.
The answer to OQ-wasm-plugin-system-19 covers only the queue half of option (a). Also answer the namespace half (Environment name as namespace).
The 'Quota denial cache' bound is a TTL (60 s per key), not a size. Give an entry bound, or state that it shares the 1,048,576-entry key table.
Order the rows by ID (CE-11 to CE-14 are interleaved) so milestone gating is easier to scan.
